description: Set up code coverage visualization in VSCode to identify untested code. Task: (1) Open Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and install a coverage visualization extension such as 'Coverage Gutters' by searching for 'Extensions: Install Extensions' then searching 'coverage gutters' or similar coverage extension. (2) Open integrated terminal (Ctrl+`) and navigate to /home/ga/workspace/coverage_task if not already there. (3) Generate coverage report by running: pytest --cov=. --cov-report=xml (this will create coverage.xml). (4) Configure the coverage extension by opening settings (Ctrl+,) and ensuring the extension can find the coverage file, or by creating/editing .vscode/settings.json in the workspace to add coverage-related configuration (e.g., 'coverage-gutters.coverageFileNames': ['coverage.xml']). (5) Activate coverage display through Command Palette (search for coverage display/watch commands) or click extension status bar icon. (6) Open calculator.py to verify coverage indicators appear in the gutter showing covered (green) and uncovered (red) lines. The workspace contains a Python project with intentional test coverage gaps - only 2 out of 5 functions in calculator.py have tests.
